source.title: [re:DEFINICIJA] Dario Kordić: Susreo sam Isusa u haaškoj tamnici (ep. 8)

summary.title_hr: [re:DEFINICIJA] Dario Kordić: Susreo sam Isusa u haaškoj tamnici (ep. 8)
summary.abstract_hr: U 8. epizodi podcasta [re:DEFINICIJA] gost je Dario Kordić, bivši dopredsjednik Hrvatske zajednice Herceg-Bosne i bivši haaški osuđenik. Govori o odrastanju u Žepču i Busovači, o braku sa suprugom Venerom, o političkoj ulozi tijekom rata u središnjoj Bosni te o svom viđenju događaja u Ahmićima. Najveći dio razgovora posvećen je njegovu odlasku u Haag 1997. godine, suđenju i kazni od 25 godina te duhovnim iskustvima u zatočeništvu, koja opisuje kao susret sa živim Bogom. Govori i o izdržavanju kazne u Grazu, izlasku na slobodu 2014. godine, studiju teologije, javnoj molitvi krunice i radu s braniteljima na rubu društva. Na kraju poručuje da Hrvatska ide u pravom smjeru ako je s Kristom.
key_topics: domovinski rat u bosni i hercegovini
key_points: Kordić je nakon demokratskih promjena bio predstojnik ureda obrane u Busovači, a zatim dopredsjednik Hrvatske zajednice Herceg-Bosne, utemeljene 18. 11. 1991. Ističe da nije bio u vojsci, nego je sebe doživljavao kao 'narodnog tribuna' i glas hrvatskih branitelja u središnjoj Bosni.

O Ahmićima tvrdi da je selo bilo vojni cilj. Navodi da je u presudi spomenuto 76 poginulih, a da su njihove procjene oko 60, te upozorava na uveličavanje brojki uz poziv na poštivanje svih žrtava s obje strane.

U Haag je otišao dobrovoljno 6. listopada 1997. Prvih 18 mjeseci opisuje kao duhovnu obnovu, a u noći prije prvog izlaska u sudnicu (12. 4. 1999.) doživio je svjetlo i čuo glas: 'Tvoju parnicu ću ja voditi.'

U prvom stupnju 2001. osuđen je na 25 godina. U žalbenom postupku skinuto mu je sedam od 21 točke, ali je kazna ostala ista. Tvrdi da mu je nova hrvatska vlast uskratila financiranje obrane, a američki odvjetnici nastavili su ga braniti bez naknade.

Nakon gotovo devet godina u Haagu kaznu je izdržavao u zatvoru Karlau u Grazu. Svjedoči da je cimer nakon dvije i pol godine njegove molitve sam uklonio sliku vraga i zamijenio je slikom Gospe. Za vrijeme izlaska u Mariazell čuo je u srcu da ide doma i pušten je 6. lipnja 2014.
Supruga Venera je, prema njegovim riječima, sama odgajala troje djece i živjela od Božje providnosti. Zahvaljujući vlasniku tvrtke Alfa dobila je posao u izdavačkoj kući.

Iz zavjeta je upisao i završio studij teologije u 60. godini. Sudjeluje u javnoj molitvi krunice, a kroz Udrugu Brat branitelj pomaže braniteljima koji su na rubu društva. Izjavu da bi 'sve ponovio' objašnjava time da bez tog puta ne bi susreo Krista.
mentioned_organizations: Međunarodni sud u Haagu za bivšu Jugoslaviju
key_topics_en: homeland war in bosnia and herzegovina
ahmići and the trial in the hague
key_points_en: After the democratic changes, Kordić was the head of the defense office in Busovača, and then vice president of the Croatian Community of Herzeg-Bosnia, founded on November 18, 1991. He emphasizes that he was not in the military, but saw himself as a 'tribune of the people' and the voice of Croatian veterans in central Bosnia.

Regarding Ahmići, he claims that the village was a military target. He states that 76 killed were mentioned in the verdict, while their estimates were around 60, and warns against exaggerating the numbers while calling for respect for all victims on both sides.

He went to The Hague voluntarily on October 6, 1997. He describes the first 18 months as a spiritual renewal, and on the night before his first appearance in the courtroom (April 12, 1999) he experienced a light and heard a voice: 'I will lead your lawsuit.'

In the first instance in 2001, he was sentenced to 25 years. In the appeals process, seven of the 21 counts were dropped, but the sentence remained the same. He claims that the new Croatian government denied him defense funding, and the American lawyers continued to defend him without compensation.

After nearly nine years in The Hague, he served his sentence in Karlau prison in Graz. He testifies that after two and a half years of his prayer, his cellmate removed a picture of the devil himself and replaced it with a picture of Our Lady. During an outing to Mariazell, he heard in his heart that he was going home, and he was released on June 6, 2014.
His wife Venera, according to his words, raised three children alone and lived on God's providence. Thanks to the owner of the company Alfa, she got a job at a publishing house.

Out of a vow, he enrolled in and completed theology studies in his 60th year. He participates in the public prayer of the Rosary, and through the Udruga Brat branitelj helps veterans who are on the margins of society. He explains his statement that he would 'repeat everything' by saying that without that path he would not have met Christ.
mentioned_organizations_en: International Court in The Hague for the former Yugoslavia
summary.title_en: [re:DEFINICIJA] Dario Kordić: I Met Jesus in the Hague Dungeon (ep. 8)
summary.abstract_en: In the 8th episode of the podcast [re:DEFINICIJA], the guest is Dario Kordić, former vice president of the Croatian Community of Herzeg-Bosnia and former Hague convict. He speaks about growing up in Žepče and Busovača, about his marriage to his wife Venera, about his political role during the war in central Bosnia, and about his view of the events in Ahmići. The largest part of the conversation is dedicated to his departure to The Hague in 1997, the trial and the 25-year sentence, and spiritual experiences in captivity, which he describes as an encounter with the living God. He also speaks about serving his sentence in Graz, his release to freedom in 2014, theology studies, the public prayer of the Rosary, and work with veterans on the margins of society. In the end, he sends the message that Croatia is moving in the right direction if it is with Christ.
